title.narrative: The Young Women for Awareness, Agency, Advocacy, and Accountability (YW4A) Programme

description.narrative: Influence the adoption, amendment, withdrawal or effective utilisation and implementation of laws and policies towards promoting young women’s rights to leadership, participation and ending SGBV in Egypt by 2025.

The programme aims to strengthen and diversify young women’s participation and amplify their voices to effectively influence decision-making towards gender-just laws, policies, norms, and practices related to their bodily integrity and equal participation.

description.narrative: Introduce anti-sexual harassment policies in the workplace to be adopted by partner WROs and other WROs and businesses in the community. Campaign for mothers to have guardianship in addition to custody rights.

comment.narrative: Calling for the creation of an accessible legally-sanctioned sex offender database would be also particularly instrumental as a monitoring and protection measure against sexual harassment and sexual assault. It is equally critical that the recent amendments are supported with proper enforcements through By-Laws that are fair, efficient, effective and equally protective.
4a) Improve existing draft law on domestic violence and lobby to be passed; campaign for mothers to have guardianship + custody rights; introduce workplace anti-sexual harassment policies

By the end of 2023, all WROs and FBO in Egypt had updated/developed their SEAH policies to match international human rights standards. Operationalization will take place in 2024, in addition to advocacy towards the ratification of ILO C190 as well.
Introduce anti-sexual harassment policies in the workplace to be adopted by partner WROs and other WROs and businesses in the community.
WROs are working on introducing improved SEAH policies in all partner organizations and ensuring conformity to ILO C190. Young women are also being trained on workplace sexual harassment.

title.narrative: WRGE 1.1 (WRG001) #of laws blocked, adopted or improved to eradicate all forms ofviolence against women and girls in public and private life;

description.narrative: Improve on the existing draft law on domestic violence and lobbying to pass it in parliament.

comment.narrative: The National Council for Women submitted to the Government a comprehensive anti-VAW bill that defines the different forms of VAW and provides a comprehensive legal framework for dealing with it. The bill has been shelved, without any indication of a serious consideration for its approval. Under YW4A, we will improve the anti-VAW law so that it:Clearly defines and criminalizes domestic violence and marital rape with deterring penalties consistent with the requirements of international instruments. The definition of rape crime should be expanded to include, besides intercourse, violating acts performed with other organs and tools. Dictate the amendment of honour crime / adultery laws to equate between men and women, starting with the abolishment of Article 237 and the equal application of standard homicide provisions on both husbands and wives. Abolished Article 60 and Article 17 allowing the judge to dismiss or reduce penalties for men on the ground of ‘honour’ and ‘good faith’ along with any legal provisions that are rooted in providing leniency for a crime committed by a man because he is a man, or because of his place within the family (typically defined as “head” or “guardian”).
A draft law is available and in 2023, WROs have created awareness amongst young women and other stakeholders on the content of the bill. It is expected to be tabled before the parliament in 2024.
Improve on the existing draft law on family law and lobbying to pass it in parliament.

WROs are creating stakeholders' awareness of the legal difference between custody and guardianship. Guardianship rights following a divorce is often a contentious issue and divorced mothers are often burdened with proving their eligible whereas, men/fathers are not required to do so.

title.narrative: WRGE 2.1 (WRG012) # of laws to promote women’s voice, agency, leadership, and representative participation in decision-making processes in public, private and civic sphere are better implemented as a result of CSO engagement.

description.narrative: Encouraging young women to run at the level of local councils and increase their participation according to the existing 25% quota.

comment.narrative: The 2014 Constitution introduced principles of full equality between men and women at all levels, including political participation and representation and guarantees women’s rights of holding public, parliamentary, and senior level positions in the State and their appointment in judicial bodies and authorities without discrimination. As a result, Egyptian women enjoy the constitutional claim to a mandated quarter of seats in both parliamentary and local elections.

The 2014 Constitution introduced principles of full equality between men and women at all levels, including political participation and representation and guarantees women’s rights of holding public, parliamentary, and senior level positions in the State and their appointment in judicial bodies and authorities without discrimination. As a result, Egyptian women enjoy the constitutional claim to a mandated quarter of seats in both parliamentary and local elections.

There were Presidential elections a the end of 2023, and YW from the project took part in civic education and actual voting as they exercised their political rights. Preparation to participate in the 2024 local council elections are ongoing.
Encouraging young women to run at the level of local councils and increase their participation according to the existing 25% quota

WROs are engaged in advocacy toward better implementation of the women's quota. The advocacy includes creating awareness amongst young women on the political structures and processes in the country and encouraging greater involvement in local councils, which also fosters women's participation in higher-level.
